newsitem.title: UK: BTR fills up water meters with Pollux buy.
newsitem.headline: BTR fills up water meters with Pollux buy.

text.p: Anglo-Australian diversified manufacturer BTR Plc said on Thursday it was to spend 163 million pounds ($261 million) on buying France's Pollux Meter Group and in doing so boost its global position in meters.

"The acquisition of PMG increases annualised sales of BTR's meters group to 330 million pounds and creates a worldwide leader in water meters with a strong presence in both the United States and Europe," the company said in a statement.

Pollux, which is a leading supplier of water meters for domestic and commercial use, has about 2,000 employees worldwide and in calendar 1996 had sales estimated at 137 million pounds, with profit before interest and tax of 16 million pounds.

BTR chief executive Ian Strachan, who started work last year on a major clean-out and reorientation at the group intended to leave the group with fewer, more dominant activities, said this deal would be a springboard for more growth in the sector.
"We intend to build on this pre-eminent position by capitalising on opportunities we have identified in product development, marketing and in growing new business in emerging markets," he said.
BTR added it planned to accelerate development of new meter technologies and related automatic meter reading systems on a global scale through product and technology transfer.
After the news BTR's share price was slightly softer in line with a weak overall market, down 1-1/2 pence at 254 pence by 0940 GMT, in volume of just over one million shares. ($1=.6237 Pound)
